acc-st-stephens-anglican-catholic-athens.assessment: St. Stephen's Anglican Catholic Church in Athens, Georgia, is a traditionalist Continuing Anglican parish of the Anglican Catholic Church (ACC). The parish uses the 1928 American Book of Common Prayer, the King James Version of Scripture, and the 1940 Hymnal as its standards of worship, and upholds male-only holy orders in continuity with the 1977 Affirmation of St. Louis.

score_notes.christology: ACC affirms the Apostles', Nicene, and Athanasian creeds; orthodox Trinitarian and Chalcedonian Christology per the 1928 BCP catechism.
score_notes.scripture: ACC upholds Article VI of the 39 Articles — Scripture as containing all things necessary to salvation; uses KJV in liturgy.
score_notes.gender: ACC restricts holy orders (bishop, priest, deacon) to qualified men only — a defining mark of the Continuing Anglican movement.
score_notes.leadership: Episcopal polity in apostolic succession; rector with vestry; male-only ordained orders.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformation Anglican soteriology per the 39 Articles, retained alongside Anglo-Catholic sacramentalism in the ACC.
score_notes.cultural: ACC was founded in 1977 (Affirmation of St. Louis) precisely to resist the Episcopal Church's ordination of women and 1979 BCP — paradigmatic confessional resistance.
score_notes.denominational: Anglican Catholic Church — founded 1977 from the Affirmation of St. Louis; uses 1928 BCP, 1940 Hymnal, KJV; one of the original Continuing Anglican jurisdictions.
score_notes.preaching: Liturgical preaching from the 1928 BCP lectionary, in the prayer-book Anglican tradition.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Vestry leadership is male; men's ministries common in ACC parishes.
score_notes.mission: ACC has a presence on six continents and nearly two dozen countries.

acna-good-shepherd-charlottesville-va.assessment: Church of the Good Shepherd is an ACNA (Diocese of the Mid-Atlantic) church plant in downtown Charlottesville, launched October 2022 under church planters Robert Cunningham and April Murrie. DOMA is the largest complementarian diocese in ACNA, ordaining only men to the priesthood. Two Sunday services (9am and 11am) at 500 Church Street. Fills a real gap as a confessional ACNA presence in Charlottesville.
